predecessors.name: Mahdist State
predecessors.text: the Sudan reconquered 1896-1898; the Mahdist remnant in Kordofan held out until the Khalifa was killed at Umm Diwaykarat in 1899

successors.name: Sudan
successors.text: the whole condominium, which became independent on 1 January 1956 (South Sudan seceded in 2011)

ledger.x: 1899: the Khalifa is run down in Kordofan.
1899 (19 January): Britain and Egypt agree to administer the Sudan jointly.
1902 (4 November): Sudan administers the Halaib land.
1910 (10 June): the Lado Enclave comes under the Sudan.
1912: the southern half of the Lado Enclave goes to Uganda.
1914 (1 January): the Sudan-Uganda boundary is settled by an exchange.
1916: Ali Dinar is killed and Darfur's resistance ends.
1934 (20 July): the Sarra triangle goes to Italian Libya.
1956 (1 January): the condominium becomes the independent Sudan.

wars.name: Mahdist War
wars.outcome: Anglo-Egyptian victory: the Khalifa Abdullah killed at Umm Diwaykarat and 'The last organised resistance from the Mahdists ended the next year' (1899).

wars.name: Anglo-Egyptian conquest of Darfur
wars.outcome: British victory: Sultan Ali Dinar killed in 1916 and Darfur incorporated (1916 on the main page, 1917 on the Darfur page).

certainty.note: The 22nd-parallel line of 1899 is a treaty line but the 1902 administrative line differs from it (Halaib); the southern and western frontiers of the Sudan with the Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and Chad are not on any page opened.
